clue.text: Love interest in adventure movie? She's enthralled

definitions.meaning: the girl in a 007 film belongs to the spy, so she is his woman
enthralled in its old sense of held in thrall, enslaved

explanation.surface: A film critic describes the romantic lead in an action film as captivated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enthralled' suggests delight, but here it means held in bondage; the first reading splits the answer into the spy's name with a possessive and a word for a female.
explanation.definitionFit: A bondswoman is a female slave or serf, and the spy James Bond's romantic partner on screen is likewise his 'woman'.

clue.text: Peculiar bulge on a sturgeon

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or strange, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notices an odd swelling on a big fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a large species of sturgeon, the source of prized caviar.

clue.text: All things considered, the French are annoying

definitions.note: the clue reads 'are annoying', a plural verb; nettle is the verb meaning to annoy

parts.note: nett, the British spelling of net, is the amount left after everything is taken into account
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A grumble that, on balance, people from France are irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stands for the verb: 'the French nettle' would replace 'the French are annoying'.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to irritate or provoke them, as the stinging plant irritates skin.

clue.text: Having drunk Pils, grannies go for a cocktail

indicators.note: drunk suggests someone tipsy and jumbled, so the letters of the three words that follow are scrambled

explanation.surface: Elderly women, after downing some lager, move on to a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like the grannies' past action with the lager; it is the anagram signal for PILS GRANNIES GO.
explanation.definitionFit: This gin-based mixed drink was created at the Raffles Hotel and is named after the island city-state.

clue.text: Charge at place for filming

definitions.meaning: a charge is an attack or assault, the beginning of an offensive
split as two words, 'at the film set' where actors are shooting a scene

explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an attack or charge, and someone 'on set' is present where a film is being shot.

clue.text: Musician first to moonwalk?

definitions.meaning: Louis ..., the jazz trumpeter and singer
Neil ..., the first person to walk on the moon, not a dancer doing the moonwalk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moonwalk' suggests the dance step made famous by Michael Jackson, another musician, but it means literally walking on the lunar surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Two famous people share this surname: the jazz trumpeter Louis and the astronaut Neil.

clue.text: Clouseau perhaps occupies most of movie

indicators.note: most of a word means all of it except its final letter

parts.note: a flick is an informal word for a film

explanation.surface: The bumbling inspector appears in nearly every scene of his film.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Clouseau is the bungling French detective of the Pink Panther films; 'most of' drops the K from FLICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Flic is French slang for a policeman, and Clouseau is a fictional French police inspector.

clue.text: He'll seduce woman unwilling with a port

parts.note: loth, a variant of loath, means reluctant
taken as written
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian seaport, is often shortened to Rio

explanation.surface: A womaniser talks a reluctant woman into running away to a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer of women, after the rake in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent.

clue.text: They may hold drink — are youngsters able to?

parts.note: can means to be able to
teens are teenagers, young people

explanation.surface: A question about whether flasks are suitable, then whether teenagers are permitted to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part reads as a question, 'can teens?', about whether young people are allowed to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Canteens are water bottles carried by soldiers or hikers, which hold drink.

clue.text: Offices provide targets for pirates without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the letters for the pirates' prey surround the other piece

parts.note: vessels carrying gold and valuables were what pirates hunted
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Some jobs offer easy pickings for buccaneers when nobody fights back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without resistance' reads as 'unopposed', the pirates meeting no fight; 'without' is the old word for outside, a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurership is the post of treasurer, an office held in a club, company or government.

clue.text: Some plutonium found in airport

indicators.note: some of a word means only part of its letters is taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Radioactive material is discovered at an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside pLUTONium; LUTON is an airport north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Luton, in Bedfordshire north of London, has a major international air terminal.

clue.text: Sort of saint taking in one with damage

definitions.text: Sort of saint taking in one with damage

indicators.note: taking in means holding something inside, so one piece is put into the other
a sort of something is a variety of it, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: A, the indefinite article, means one
to mar is to spoil or damage

explanation.surface: A kind of holy person welcomes someone who has been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' is the anagram signal and 'taking in' the container; the whole clue also describes the parable of the Good Samaritan tending the injured traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: In the parable, the Good Samaritan cares for a robbed and beaten stranger, so the name means a charitable helper.

clue.text: Noble with ill-will to member of army

parts.note: gall is bitterness or rancour
army ants march in vast columns, so an ant is a member of an army

explanation.surface: An aristocrat feels resentment towards a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of army' suggests a soldier; it is an insect from a column of army ants.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant means brave and chivalrous, as a noble knight is.

clue.text: Wood, pine's sound — one may toast it

indicators.note: sound tells us that the words before it are said aloud to give the answer

parts.note: teak is a hardwood and to pine is to ache, so the pair said together is teak-ache

explanation.surface: A carpenter notes the noise a timber makes, then talks about toasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like another wood beside teak, but it is the verb meaning to long or ache; TEAK ACHE said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a light sweet bun with currants, usually split, toasted and buttered.

clue.text: TV serial the answer for film producer

parts.note: a soap is a long-running television drama serial
a solution is the answer to a problem or puzzle

explanation.surface: A long-running drama is just what a movie mogul needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film producer' suggests a movie mogul, but the liquid produces a thin film, as in blowing bubbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapy water forms a thin film, the skin of a bubble, when stretched across a loop.

clue.text: Legislator comes in to support man's climbing plant

indicators.note: comes in means enters, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pier is a pillar that supports a bridge or arch
MP stands for Member of Parliament, a legislator

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Len is a man's name

explanation.surface: A politician props up somebody's creeping garden flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing plant' looks like the definition, but 'climbing' is the reversal signal for the man's name, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is a small wild flower with red petals that close in dull weather.

clue.text: Dinosaur wanting capital punishment almost on demand

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: the rope, meaning hanging, is a form of execution
O/D is the banking abbreviation for on demand

explanation.surface: A fossil creature calls for execution, more or less immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims THE ROPE to THE ROP, and OD follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Theropods were the two-legged meat-eating dinosaurs, such as Tyrannosaurus.

clue.text: Mine's terrible place for fragile material

parts.note: egg was old military slang for a mine or bomb, with the 's kept as the S
hell is a dreadful place

explanation.surface: A minefield is described as an awful place for something delicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine's' looks like a possessive pronoun or a colliery; it is EGG, slang for an explosive mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell is a thin, brittle covering, so it stands for anything delicate and easily broken.

clue.text: Secret proposal in Cameron's speech?

definitions.meaning: done in a concealed or clandestine way
David Cameron's 2006 speech urging people to 'hug a hoodie' is recast as hug a mugger

explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron, later UK Prime Minister, gave a 2006 speech urging understanding of hooded youths, mocked as 'hug a hoodie'; 'hug a mugger' says the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugger-mugger means secretive or concealed, and also confused or muddled.

clue.text: A coin's wasted here?

indicators.note: wasted suggests ruined or squandered, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is read as a plural, coins

explanation.surface: A gambler watches a coin thrown away at the tables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' rearranges A COINS; the whole clue describes a gambling house where money is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a gambling venue, where stakes are often lost.

clue.text: Platform — one for English in upper classes

indicators.note: one thing for another means a swap, so the letter for one replaces the letter for English

parts.note: the gentry are the people of high social rank
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A stage where a foreigner swaps places with an Englishman among the posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One for English' swaps the E of GENTRY for A.
explanation.definitionFit: A gantry is a raised framework or platform, such as one carrying cranes or rail signals.

clue.text: Decide to answer clue again

definitions.meaning: to make up one's mind firmly
..., to work out the answer a second time

explanation.definitionFit: To resolve is to settle firmly on a course, and with a hyphen it means solving once more.

clue.text: Cosmetic old lady has to cover a blemish

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the outer letters enclose the mark

parts.note: ma is informal for mother, someone's old lady
taken as written
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: An elderly woman uses make-up to hide a flaw on her face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has to cover' looks like the old lady hiding a mark; it says the outer letters enclose the blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is make-up applied to darken and thicken the eyelashes.

clue.text: Dignitary dressing right

parts.note: mayo is short for mayonnaise, a salad dressing

explanation.surface: A civic official puts on the correct clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests putting on robes of office; it is salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the elected civic head of a town or city, a local dignitary.

clue.text: Woman following 1996/7 car for a time carrying a child

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the woman's name is placed after the car

parts.note: UK number plates registered from August 1996 to July 1997 began with P, so such a car is P-reg
Nancy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman trails an old car around for a while with a baby on board.
explanation.walkthrough: British number plates once began with a year letter; a car from 1996/7 is 'P-reg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pregnancy is the period during which a woman carries a developing baby.

clue.text: Gull — one I point out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: out here means on the outside, so the word for point goes round the letter

parts.note: a dot is a point
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gestures at a seabird, saying 'that's mine'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gull' suggests the seabird but means a dupe; 'out' puts DOT outside the second I to make DIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is someone easily fooled, a simpleton or fool.

clue.text: Give out grief

definitions.meaning: an archaic and poetic word for sorrow or lamentation

explanation.definitionFit: To dole is to hand out sparingly, and in old poetry dole also meant sorrow or mourning.

clue.text: Ely rector's arranged high position in church

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters of the cathedral city and the priest are reordered

parts.note: the possessive is read as plain letters with its S

explanation.surface: A clergyman in the cathedral city of Ely has organised a senior church post.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is an English cathedral city; 'arranged' rearranges ELY RECTORS. 'High position' suggests a senior job, but it is a part of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerestory is the upper row of windows in a church nave, set high above the aisle roofs.
